memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for advanced packaging/HBM integration, but later layers must test whether AI/HBM revenue is material versus broad packaging exposure.
FORM is a strong underfollowed candidate for HBM/advanced-packaging test because known-good-die and fine-pitch interposer verification are direct chokepoint-adjacent functions.
KLIC is a candidate for advanced-packaging equipment scarcity through thermocompression bonding, especially where AI, CPO, HPC, and heterogeneous integration overlap.

AEHR is a speculative-shadow candidate: direct AI processor test/burn-in orders exist, but survival through later layers depends on revenue materiality, customer concentration, and repeat-order durability.

This pass did not fully cover US-listed materials suppliers for underfill, thermal interface materials, ABF substrate exposure, or inspection/metrology beyond the selected names; these should be a follow-up Layer 1B subpass.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM integration, leading-edge foundry, and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the advanced-packaging/HBM/test chokepoint with a two-lane list. AMKR is included as the reference OSAT anchor. FORM, KLIC, and AEHR are underfollowed or lower-attention equipment/test candidates tied to HBM known-good-die testing, thermocompression bonding for heterogeneous integration/co-packaged optics, and wafer/package-level burn-in for AI processors. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation. Later layers must verify AI revenue materiality, customer concentration, order durability, capacity constraints, and whether the market has already priced the bottleneck.
